analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (24.11.2026)
key_insights: Nvidia board reinstated Jensen Huang after input from US government officials, stating no national security risk. GS sees it as positive for NVDA and the AI ecosystem, but SEC investigations remain an overhang until resolved or more disclosure is given.
GS retains Buy on Nvidia with $220 price target based on 22X P/E on $10 EPS, citing positive risk/reward.

Bill Ackman argues another Fed hike would raise recession risk and sees 3% inflation as more realistic given geopolitics, defense spending, tariffs, less globalized supply chains and AI infrastructure and power demand.
Ackman cited credit stress example: SpaceX issued $25bn secured debt at over 8% vs unsecured debt of same 2033 maturity at 5.65% in June.
HPE said on its call that AI is creating reasons to expand on-premises and private cloud infrastructure after nearly two decades of public cloud migration.

GS sentiment indicator fell to the 36th percentile, lowest since Liberation Day. Lower positioning has historically meant better forward equity return asymmetry, and fund flows have stayed resilient despite higher volatility.
Tech selloff drove a sharp reset in positioning and liquidity. Fast money de-risking accelerated while retail moved the opposite way.

GS TMT spec sales frame bulls as expecting a rally on nobody-left-to-sell positioning and a sentiment-driven AI/Semis bear market, while bears cite China, permitting, ROI and token trajectory questions and difficulty rallying above pre-Election levels.

BTC hit a new cycle low of $55.3k before rebounding, with about $1.4bn of perp liquidations over the weekend and a 200-dma break. ETF outflows have nearly erased net flows since the 19 August rally began, and on-chain metrics approach stress levels.
GS reiterates Buy on Amazon with $370 12-month target, calling it the most compelling risk/reward in mega/large cap coverage, with AWS growth supportive and strategic shifts in Commerce.

European Staples (GSXESTAP) had their best month on record in October. GS likes selling Staples on rich valuation, unexciting earnings and low dividend yield vs fixed income, and US colleagues also sell the sector.
GS prefers equities to credit given tight spreads, releveraging and rising issuance. Late-1990s analog suggests equities can keep rising with more volatility while credit lags.

Stat of the day: since 1952 across 18 midterms, S&P 500 averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over the following 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months after the election. S&P earnings run well above multi-decade trend.
